To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a meiobenthically dominated ichnofabric composed mainly of Virgaichnuss undulatus igen et isp nov. and Hydrancyluss isp. is described from the Late Permian of the Oman Mountains.

(1) a meiobenthos ichnofabric from the Saiq Formation in the Oman Mountains is dominated by Virgaichnites undulatus igen., et isp. nov.; (2) this ichnofabric represents the first record of Virgaichnita from the Arabian Plate, which is the first record of meiobentic ichnofossils from the Arabian Plate; (3) Virgaichnitus undulatus igen, et isp. nov., and

the ichnofabric is composed of miniature ichnofossils, which are diagnostic for the ichnogenus Virgaichnussp. nov., that these ichnofossils are interpreted as worm-like burrowers and that the ichnofossils indicate an upper shoreface to lower shoreface environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ichnofabric of a Late Permian carbonate platform and its meiobenthos.
a new ichnotaxon, the ichnofabric it creates, the potential trace maker(s) and their ecological significance.
the description of a new trace fossil, the interpretation of its trace maker and the implications of the trace maker for palaeoenvironments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
V. undulatos is produced by a nemertean worm.
Virgaichnuss undulatus igen., isp. nov. is produced by a vermiform, worm-like organism.
the ichnofabric is the result of a complex, multi-species assemblage of meiobenths.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ichnofabric of V. undulatos is a good indicator of a shallow subtidal to intertidal environment.
ichnofabric studies of meiobenths can provide important palaeoenvironment information, which can be used as a complementary tool to other proxies in carbonate rocks.
the ichnofabric described here is a miniature version of the large ichnofabric described from the Late Permian of Oman by Fürsich and Oschmann (2002).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of morphology and size of meiobentic trace fossils can be used for the interpretation of trace makers and consequently strengthens the potential of meiobenths in palaeoenvironment and facies analysis.

ichnofabrics composed of meiobicnthic trace fossils are not uncommon in the fossil record, and their study is a promising tool to gain insights into the evolution of meiofauna and their ecological significance.
the combination of morphology and size is a powerful tool to unravel the trace maker and its palaeoenvironment.
